title: Categorized Free Recall with Closed-Loop Stimulation at Encoding (Encoding Classifier)
description: This dataset comprises intracranial EEG recordings and behavioral events from a categorized free recall task with closed-loop electrical stimulation applied during encoding. Participants studied word lists organized by semantic category, performed arithmetic distractor tasks, and freely recalled words, while a classifier trained on prior encoding data determined stimulation delivery based on predicted memory encoding success. Data were collected across multiple clinical sites in collaboration with the Computational Memory Lab at the University of Pennsylvania, as part of the DARPA Restoring Active Memory (RAM) project.
methods_description: Intracranial EEG was recorded during a categorized free recall task involving word list encoding, arithmetic distraction, and free recall. Closed-loop stimulation was delivered to a single electrode during encoding when an L2 logistic regression classifier, trained on spectral power features (Morlet wavelet transform, 3-180 Hz, 60 Hz line noise removed via Butterworth filter) from prior catFR1 sessions, predicted low likelihood of subsequent recall. Classifier performance was validated via leave-one-session-out cross-validation with permutation testing, and stimulation thresholds were set using Youden's J statistic. Recordings were labeled as monopolar or bipolar, with electrode locations provided in MNI and Talairach coordinates.
